title: Stop-block catapult
goal_text: The arm is cocked away from the stop post, then the motor drives it back. The striker slams the post, the arm halts, and the ball leaves the cup and flies over the post. Place the ball's first ground contact at the requested x coordinate (it lands on the negative-x side). Choose how far the arm is cocked and how hard the motor pushes.
manual:
Device 'stop_catapult' (9 parts). Coordinates in metres, z up, ground at z=0. Joint coordinates are 0 in the pose described here.
Parts:
- column: box 0.080 x 0.100 x 0.620 m, concrete, mass 11.904 kg; centre (0.000, 0.000, 0.310), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (-0.040, -0.050, 0.000)..(0.040, 0.050, 0.620); rests on the ground, fixed in place
- axle: cylinder radius 0.008 m, length 0.120 m, steel, mass 0.189 kg; centre (0.000, 0.060, 0.620), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (1.571, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (-0.008, 0.000, 0.612)..(0.008, 0.120, 0.628); rigidly fixed to 'column'
- arm: capsule radius 0.012 m, length 0.160 m, wood, mass 0.052 kg; centre (0.000, 0.100, 0.700), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (-0.012, 0.088, 0.608)..(0.012, 0.112, 0.792); hinge joint to 'axle' at (0.000, 0.100, 0.620), axis (0.000, 1.000, 0.000), bearing model, end stops [-0.600, 1.450] rad
- cup: box 0.044 x 0.044 x 0.010 m, wood, mass 0.013 kg; centre (0.000, 0.100, 0.798), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (-0.022, 0.078, 0.793)..(0.022, 0.122, 0.803); rigidly fixed to 'arm'
- lip: box 0.010 x 0.044 x 0.036 m, wood, mass 0.010 kg; centre (0.025, 0.100, 0.819), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (0.020, 0.078, 0.801)..(0.030, 0.122, 0.837); rigidly fixed to 'cup'
- striker: box 0.016 x 0.090 x 0.028 m, wood, mass 0.026 kg; centre (0.000, 0.150, 0.720), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (-0.008, 0.105, 0.706)..(0.008, 0.195, 0.734); rigidly fixed to 'arm'
- slug: box 0.044 x 0.056 x 0.044 m, steel, sealed, mass unknown (between 0.05 and 0.25 kg); centre (0.034, 0.100, 0.690), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (0.012, 0.072, 0.668)..(0.056, 0.128, 0.712); rigidly fixed to 'arm'
- stop_post: box 0.040 x 0.060 x 0.750 m, concrete, mass 4.320 kg; centre (-0.040, 0.160, 0.375), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (-0.060, 0.130, 0.000)..(-0.020, 0.190, 0.750); rests on the ground, fixed in place
- ball: sphere radius 0.016 m, steel, sealed, mass unknown (between 0.02 and 0.1 kg); centre (0.000, 0.100, 0.820), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (-0.016, 0.084, 0.804)..(0.016, 0.116, 0.836); loose (free body), carried by 'cup' when it is set up
Actuators (command in [-1, 1]):
- drive: motor_large driving 'arm'
Sensors (Gaussian noise, standard deviation):
- arm_angle: joint_angle of 'arm', noise 0.002
- arm_rate: joint_velocity of 'arm', noise 0.01
- ball_speed: velocity of 'ball', noise 0.01
- ball_where: position of 'ball', noise 0.002
Visual markers:
- target: at (-1.050, 0.100, 0.000), radius 0.050 m
Physics: rigid bodies with soft contacts, gravity 9.81 m/s^2 along -z. Contact friction between two surfaces is the larger of their two coefficients. Unknowns of scope 'world' are properties of a material or of a catalog part model (bearing, rail, spring, motor type): they are identical in every device and every instance in this world. Unknowns of scope 'device' belong to this device and are drawn anew for every instance.
Before each run: joint of 'arm' is set to knob 'cock'
Action program (then all commands 0 until the end): phase 0: lasts 2 s; commands [drive = knob 'power']

knobs.name: cock
knobs.description: arm start angle, cocked away from the stop post

knobs.name: power
knobs.description: motor command held during the throw; it is negative because that is the direction that drives the arm toward the stop post

unknowns.name: ball_mass
unknowns.description: mass of the sealed launch ball

unknowns.name: slug_mass
unknowns.description: mass of the sealed slug clamped to the arm

outcome.description: the x coordinate(s) of 'ball' at the moment it first touches the ground

rules:
Protocol (enforced by the lab tool):
1. Pretest: you get 3 goals one at a time and must choose knob values for each
   before running any experiment on this device. Results are revealed only at the end.
2. Lab: up to 80 experiments. Every experiment requires your prediction of the
   outcome before you see the result. Every 10th experiment is chosen by the referee:
   you are told the knob values, you predict, then you see the result.
3. Theory: submit predict.py defining predict(knobs: dict, visible: dict) -> list[float],
   your model of the outcome. `visible` holds the modifiable dimensions listed below; the
   referee may evaluate your model with different values for them, without letting you
   experiment. Also submit your estimates of the unknown quantities with 90% intervals.
4. Exam: 8 goals one at a time, one attempt each, no experiments. Results are
   revealed only at the end.
5. Field report: optional tickets about the interface (bugs, ambiguity, suspected
   unsolvability). Tickets go to the device builder; they cannot contain answers.
Outcome is a failure if the run status is not "ok" (e.g. the part never landed, or was
still moving at the end of the run).
